page: Amazon Web Services g5g.xlarge is an accelerated computing instance configured with an AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 arm64 processor delivering 4 dedicated physical cores (4 vCPUs) clocked at 2.5 GHz. The CPU architecture includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, backed by 8.0 GB of system memory at an allocation of 2.0 GB per core. Acceleration is provided by a bundled discrete NVIDIA T4G GPU with 16 GB of VRAM. Operating on the Nitro hypervisor, the instance provides a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth and includes no local instance storage, requiring network-attached storage volumes for data persistence.

Benchmark measurements place general compute and memory throughput in modest performance brackets compared across broader cloud hardware. Single-core compute registered an average rating in stress-ng with a score of 1519.58, whereas multi-core stress-ng reached 6054.45 and Geekbench multi-core scored 3155.0. Memory bandwidth evaluation recorded 72.22 GB/sec on large uncached read blocks and 34.75 GB/sec on write blocks. In small language model benchmarking (135M model), prompt processing completed at 113.08 tokens per second and text generation reached 49.02 tokens per second.

Pairing an energy-efficient ARM processor with an NVIDIA Turing-generation GPU yields a resource profile oriented around hardware efficiency for GPU-bound pipelines that do not demand high x86 instruction overhead. Tradeoffs include a limited system memory capacity of 8.0 GB and the absence of high-speed local disk storage. The g5g.xlarge is suited for Android cloud gaming, video encoding, computer vision workloads, and lightweight machine learning inference.
description: Amazon Web Services g5g.xlarge is an accelerated computing virtual machine that combines AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 arm64 architecture with dedicated graphics hardware. Running on the Nitro hypervisor, it features 4 physical cores and 4 vCPUs clocked at 2.5 GHz, 8.0 GB of system memory, and a baseline network throughput of 1 Gbps. It integrates a dedicated NVIDIA T4G GPU featuring 16 GB of VRAM, with zero local storage bundled. Benchmark evaluations reflect average single-thread performance alongside modest multi-core compute metrics, recording 1519.58 in single-core stress-ng and 3155.0 in Geekbench multi-core tests. While its 2.0 GB of memory per core and absence of local disks constrain data-heavy enterprise applications, the arm64 and Turing GPU combination delivers hardware efficiency for cost-sensitive accelerated tasks. The instance is suited for Android application streaming, graphics rendering, media transcoding, and lightweight machine learning inference.
